AnsiHandler final class

Collects ANSI parse events into a flat list of Segments.

MethodSummary
parse(string $input): arrayParse a complete input in one shot: feed every byte, then finalise.
feed(string $input): voidFeed bytes through the state machine, accumulating segments.
finish(): voidEnd of stream: force any in-flight string sequence to dispatch and finalise the dangling tail.
reset(): voidReset all accumulated state (segments, text buffer, flags). Used by StreamingInspector between sessions.
drainSegments(): arrayReturn all segments produced since the last drain (or since reset). Does NOT call flushText() — pending text is only flushed when a sequence dispatch auto-flushes (csiDispatch / oscDispatch / etc.) or when finish() is called. This preserves the streaming invariant that text is returned only when a sequence is completed or the stream ends.

Inspector final class

Walk a string of mixed text + ANSI escape sequences and split it into Segments. The decoder labels SGR codes (foreground, background, attributes), CSI cursor moves, CSI erase/mode toggles, OSC titles, and bracketed-paste / focus / mouse mode sequences. Anything it doesn't recognise still gets a Segment with a generic "CSI" / "OSC" / "SS3" label, so no sequence that reaches the segmenter is dropped without a report. Bytes can still vanish further upstream, inside sugar-ansi-parser, before this code ever sees a dispatch — README.md keeps the closed list of every known case and ByteFidelityTest pins each one.

MethodSummary
static parse(string $input): arrayParse $input into a list of segments. Plain text becomes TextSegment; escape sequences become SequenceSegment.
static report(string $input, bool $showOffsets = false): stringRender parsed segments as a sequin-style report (one per line).
static formatSegment(Segment $seg, bool $showOffsets = false): stringOne report line for a segment: its describe() rendering, prefixed with the hex byte offset when $showOffsets is set and the segment carries a stream position (segments hand-constructed outside a parse are untracked and render without a prefix).
static reportAsJson(string $input): stringRender parsed segments as a machine-readable JSON array.
static encodeSegmentsJson(iterable $segments): stringJSON projection of an already-parsed segment list — the shared body of reportAsJson() and the bin's --json streaming arm (finding 005: a pipe under --json collects segments and encodes the same array shape).
static describeCsi(string $params, string $final): string
static describeMouseX10(string $payload): stringX10 mouse event (finding 006): the three raw bytes that trail ESC[M, each offset by 32. Low bits 0-2 select button (3 = release), bit 4 shift, bit 8 meta, bit 16 ctrl, bit 5 drag, the 64 band wheels; coordinates are byte-minus-31 (1-based).
static describeOsc(string $payload): string
static describeDcs(string $payload, int $final = 0): stringDecode DCS payloads — XTVERSION reply, DECRQSS, DECRPSS, sixel, tmux passthrough.
static describeDcsParts(int $final, array $params, int $prefix, int $intermediate, string $data, string $rawPayload = ''): stringClassify a DCS body from the parser's true dispatch fields using the shared Dcs decoder, rendering the label in this inspector's house spelling: attacker-controlled payload bytes go through sanitizeLabelBytes() (named C0/C1 tokens), the same discipline as the OSC/APC labels, so a captured reply can't inject control bytes into the inspector's own output.
static describeApc(string $payload): stringDecode APC payloads — CandyZone markers, kitty graphics.
static describeSs3(string $final): string
static describeEsc(string $byte, string $intermediate = ''): stringNames a two- or three-byte ESC sequence. The intermediate byte (the 0x20–0x2F the EscapeIntermediate state collects, finding 014) changes the final byte's meaning entirely — ESC 8 is DECRC while ESC # 8 is DECALN — so the bare-ESC arms are gated on its absence and an unexpected intermediate never borrows a bare label.
static describeTruncated(string $bytes): stringLabel a sequence the stream never terminated (ECMA-48 §5.6 escape sequences run introducer → parameters → intermediates → final byte, and the final byte is what completes them).
static sanitizeLabelBytes(string $s): stringReplace C0, DEL and C1 control bytes in a label interpolation with visible tokens.

Lang final class

Segment abstract class

Base class for the chunks produced by Inspector::parse(). Every segment can both render itself verbatim (raw()) and produce a human-readable description (describe()).

MethodSummary
abstract raw(): string
abstract describe(): string
abstract byteOffset(): ?intAbsolute byte offset where this segment starts in the parsed input, or null for a segment that was hand-constructed and therefore carries no stream position (finding 019 — the location sequin prints beside every decoded entry).

SequenceSegment final class

One ANSI escape sequence — its raw bytes paired with a decoded label (e.g. "SGR foreground red"). The label is what makes CandyAnsiInspect useful as a debugging tool: you can pipe styled output in and see exactly which sequence produced what effect.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $bytes, public readonly string $label, public readonly ?int $offset = null)The raw bytes are stored verbatim; the report renders them through printable(), which tokenizes every control byte.
raw(): string
byteOffset(): ?int
describe(): string
static printable(string $bytes): stringRender bytes with control bytes replaced by visible tokens: \x1b becomes ESC, every C0/DEL/C1 byte becomes its named token (CR, BEL, RI, …), and printable ASCII plus well-formed UTF-8 runes survive verbatim.

SugarCraft\AnsiInspect\Support

Version final class

The version string this tool reports on --version.

MethodSummary
static line(): stringThe --version line: plain text, newline-terminated, produced by no state and no host probe — the flag must answer anywhere.
static current(): stringThe version this process reports: the archive stamp when running from a stamped phar, self::CURRENT everywhere else.
static fromPharMetadata(string $path): ?stringThe version a phar archive at $path was built to carry, or null when it names none (unreadable archive, wrong metadata shape, the dev-build sentinel, or an empty stamp). Every refusal is a null, never an exception — --version must answer on a machine whose phar cannot be opened.
static versionFromMetadata(mixed $metadata): ?stringThe judgement on the stamp itself, split out because the archive-open leg is unreachable from a suite that must not build phars: the release namespace strip, the dev-build refusal, and the wrong-type nulls are a pure function over what getMetadata() answers.
static hostArchive(): stringThe filesystem path of the phar this process was launched from, or '' when it was not launched from one — the two-identity law measured on candy-code's real builds and pinned by the bin autoload guard: inside archive-loaded code Phar::running(false) answers the archive path, while the stub context answers '' and there a '.phar'-suffixed __DIR__ is the enclosing archive.
